title: Protocols & Ports
subtitle: TCP vs UDP, the exam port table, mail chain, web/file transfer & support protocols

readingSections.title: What Are Network Protocols?
readingSections.quickSummary: Agreed rule-sets that let devices communicate; each protocol has a job (mail, web, files, names) and most have a fixed port number.
content: A protocol is an agreed set of rules governing communication between devices - message format, order, and actions on send/receive. Protocols are layered: low-level ones move raw bits (TCP/IP), higher-level ones define applications (HTTP fetches pages, SMTP sends mail).

For the exam, protocols reduce to two tables: WHO does WHAT (protocol-to-purpose matching) and WHICH PORT (a 16-bit number identifying the application on a machine). Well-known ports run 0-1023; the exam draws from about a dozen.
Ports let one machine run many services at once: the IP address finds the machine, the port finds the program on it. That 'IP = street, port = flat number' picture answers half of all port questions.

subsections.title: The protocol families
subsections.content:
Transport: TCP (reliable) and UDP (fast).
Web: HTTP (plain), HTTPS (TLS-encrypted).
Mail: SMTP (send), POP3/IMAP (retrieve).
Files: FTP (insecure), SFTP/FTPS (secure), TFTP (trivial UDP).
Support: DNS (names), DHCP (address leasing), ICMP (ping/errors), SNMP (management), Telnet/SSH (remote terminals).

subsections.title: Why ports matter
subsections.content: A server listening on port 80 serves web pages; port 25 serves mail. A client picks an ephemeral (temporary) port for its side. Firewalls filter by port - which is exactly how the AXIS ACL questions work: 'permit tcp any host 1.1.1.1 eq smtp'.

quickRevision: Protocol = communication rule-set; layered like the network model.
IP finds the machine; PORT finds the program.
Well-known ports = 0-1023; memorise the exam dozen.
Every protocol has a one-line purpose - match stems to purposes.
tricks: Port pairs with meaning: 22 SSH (secure shell), 23 Telnet (INSECURE shell) - exams swap them.
80 vs 443: plain vs padlock. 443 = HTTPS = TLS.
Mail trio: 25 send, 110 POP3 fetch-delete, 143 IMAP fetch-keep.
DNS rides UDP 53 for queries (TCP 53 for zone transfers).
patterns: 'Which port does X use?' - table recall.
'Which protocol for Y purpose?' - purpose matching.

pyqPatterns.question: Permit SMTP mail to only host 1.1.1.1.
pyqPatterns.approach: Extended ACL: access-list 110 permit tcp any host 1.1.1.1 eq smtp - protocol + port in one line.

readingSections.companyNote: Port-matching questions appear in nearly every networking bucket across TCS, Accenture and Cocubes papers.

readingSections.title: TCP vs UDP: Reliable vs Fast
readingSections.quickSummary: TCP: connection-oriented, ordered, retransmits - reliable but heavier. UDP: connectionless datagrams - fast, no delivery guarantee.
content: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is CONNECTION-ORIENTED: a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) opens a session, sequence numbers keep data ordered, and acknowledgements trigger retransmission of anything lost. Reliable, but that bookkeeping costs time and headers.

UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is CONNECTIONLESS: fire-and-forget datagrams with no handshake, no ordering, no retry. Minimal overhead makes it perfect for DNS lookups, live video/voice, gaming and broadcasts - anywhere speed beats perfection.
Choosing between them is a standard MCQ: web pages, email and file transfer need TCP's reliability; streaming, DNS queries and VoIP prefer UDP's speed.

subsections.title: The three-way handshake
subsections.content:
Client -> SYN ('let's talk?').
Server -> SYN-ACK ('yes, and here's my number').
Client -> ACK ('confirmed') - connection established, data flows.
Teardown uses FIN/ACK exchanges.

subsections.title: Who rides on what
subsections.content:
TCP: HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, SSH, Telnet.
UDP: DNS queries, DHCP, TFTP, SNMP, VoIP, video streaming, online games.
DNS is the classic split case: queries on UDP 53, zone transfers on TCP 53.

quickRevision: UDP = connectionless, unordered, no retry, lighter/faster.
tricks: 'Handshake / acknowledgement / ordered delivery' in the stem -> TCP, every time.
Live video lagging but complete = TCP; live video dropping frames = UDP - exams frame this as 'which for streaming?'
DNS default transport is UDP - a favourite trick question.

pyqPatterns.question: Difference between TCP and UDP?
pyqPatterns.approach: Connection-oriented + reliable vs connectionless + fast; pick the option with BOTH halves right.

readingSections.companyNote: One TCP/UDP comparison question appears in almost every technical MCQ paper ever set.

readingSections.title: The Mail Chain: SMTP, POP3, IMAP
readingSections.quickSummary: SMTP sends and relays (25); POP3 downloads-and-deletes (110); IMAP keeps mail server-side and syncs (143).
content: Email travels in one direction protocol and arrives via another. SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, port 25) PUSHES mail: client-to-server and server-to-server. It never retrieves.

POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3, port 110) PULLS mail by downloading it to ONE device, typically deleting the server copy - simple but breaks multi-device use. IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol, port 143) keeps mail ON the server and synchronises folders across every device - the modern default.
Secure variants ride TLS: SMTPS (465/587), POP3S (995), IMAPS (993). Exam stems test the send-vs-retrieve split and the POP3-vs-IMAP sync difference.

subsections.title: Flow example
subsections.content:
Alice (Gmail) writes to Bob (Outlook):
1. Alice's client -> Gmail server via SMTP.
2. Gmail server -> Outlook server via SMTP (server-to-server relay).
3. Bob's devices fetch via IMAP (server-side sync) or POP3 (download).

quickRevision: SMTP = send/relay (25). POP3 = download/delete (110). IMAP = server-side sync (143).
tricks: 'S' = Send in SMTP - the only SENDING protocol of the three.
POP3's P = Post Office: collect your letter and leave the box empty (server copy deleted).
IMAP's I = Internet: mail stays on the Internet server, synced everywhere.
patterns: 'Read the same mailbox on phone and laptop' - IMAP.
'Downloads messages and removes them from the server' - POP3.

pyqPatterns.question: ACL permitting SMTP to one host.
pyqPatterns.approach: eq smtp in an extended ACL - port 25 semantics.

readingSections.companyNote: Mail-protocol matching is a recurring one-mark question - the send/retrieve split is the whole answer.

readingSections.title: Web & File Transfer: HTTP(S), FTP, SFTP
readingSections.quickSummary: HTTP fetches pages in plaintext (80); HTTPS wraps it in TLS (443); FTP moves files unencrypted (20/21); SFTP tunnels over SSH (22).
content: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, port 80) is the request-response language of the web: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE. It is PLAINTEXT - anyone on the path can read it. HTTPS = HTTP inside TLS encryption on port 443: confidentiality, integrity and server authentication via certificates.

FTP (File Transfer Protocol) moves files using two channels - control on port 21, data on port 20 - with credentials in CLEARTEXT. Secure replacements: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol over port 22, encrypted) and FTPS (FTP over TLS). TFTP (Trivial FTP, UDP 69) is a minimal no-auth version for LAN bootstrapping.

Remote terminals: Telnet (23) predates security - everything typed, including passwords, travels in plaintext; SSH (22) is its encrypted replacement. 'Secure replacement for Telnet/FTP' is a ready-made MCQ pair.

subsections.title: HTTP methods worth knowing
subsections.content:
GET - retrieve a resource (parameters in URL).
POST - submit data (body).
PUT - upload/replace.
DELETE - remove.
Status codes: 200 OK, 301 redirect, 404 not found, 500 server error.

subsections.title: HTTPS certificates
subsections.content: TLS handshake: server presents a certificate signed by a Certificate Authority; the browser verifies the chain, then both derive session keys. That is how the browser 'authenticates' the site - the published PYQ pairing with user logins.

tricks: FTP's TWO ports (21 control, 20 data) - exams love asking which is which.
'Credentials in plaintext' -> Telnet or HTTP or FTP; the secure twins are SSH, HTTPS, SFTP.

pyqPatterns.question: FTP uses which two ports?
pyqPatterns.approach: 21 control, 20 data - order matters in the options.

readingSections.companyNote: HTTP-vs-HTTPS and FTP port questions are permanent fixtures of technical MCQ rounds.

readingSections.title: Support Protocols: DNS, DHCP, ARP, ICMP, SNMP
readingSections.quickSummary: DNS translates names to IPs (53); DHCP leases addresses via DORA; ARP maps IP to MAC; ICMP carries ping/errors; SNMP manages devices.
content: DNS (Domain Name System, port 53) translates human names (google.com) into IP addresses through a hierarchy: resolver -> root -> TLD (.com) -> authoritative server. Queries ride UDP 53; zone transfers between servers use TCP 53.
DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) leases IP configuration to hosts through DORA: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge - all broadcast initially. Leases expire and renew automatically.

ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) answers 'who has this IP?' inside a LAN, mapping IPv4 to MAC. ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is ping's transport - echo request/reply plus error messages (destination unreachable, TTL exceeded). SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol, UDP 161) monitors and manages network devices.

subsections.title: DORA in one line each
subsections.content:
Discover - client broadcasts 'any DHCP server?'.
Offer - server offers an address.
Request - client formally asks for the offered address.
Acknowledge - server confirms the lease.

quickRevision: DNS 53 (UDP queries / TCP transfers) - names to IPs.
ARP - IP to MAC on the LAN. ICMP - ping and errors.
tricks: DORA order mnemonic: the word DORA itself - Discover Offer Request Ack.
ping = ICMP, not UDP/TCP - a trick option in every paper.
DNS over UDP by default; 'zone transfer' flips it to TCP.
patterns: 'Translates domain names to IP addresses' - DNS.
'Maps IP address to MAC address' - ARP.
readingSections.companyNote: DNS/DHCP/ARP purpose-matching questions recur in every networking bucket - four definitions, four free marks.

formulas.title: TCP vs UDP Decision Table

formula.text: Reliability apps ride TCP; realtime lookups/streams ride UDP.

explanation: TCP: handshake, sequencing, ACKs, retransmission - HTTP(S), FTP, SMTP, SSH.
UDP: no handshake/order/retry - DNS queries, DHCP, TFTP, VoIP, streaming, gaming.
DNS is the split case: UDP 53 queries, TCP 53 zone transfers.
Overhead: TCP header 20+ bytes vs UDP 8 bytes.

example.prompt: Which transport carries a live video call?

formulas.memoryTip: TCP = Tracked, Checked, Patient. UDP = Untracked, Direct, Prompt.
formulas.commonMistake: Putting DNS on TCP by default - queries ride UDP 53.

formulas.title: The Exam Port Table

formula.latex: 20/21\text{ FTP}, 22\text{ SSH}, 23\text{ Telnet}, 25\text{ SMTP}, 53\text{ DNS}, 69\text{ TFTP}, 80\text{ HTTP}, 110\text{ POP3}, 143\text{ IMAP}, 443\text{ HTTPS}
formula.text: Twelve ports cover every placement question ever set on this.

explanation: FTP splits 21 control / 20 data.
SSH 22 replaced Telnet 23 - one number apart, security worlds apart.
Mail: 25 send, 110 POP3, 143 IMAP (secure: 465/587, 995, 993).
Web: 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS. DNS 53, TFTP 69 (UDP), SNMP 161, RDP 3389.
formulas.memoryTip: 21-22-23: FTP, SSH, Telnet in a row - middle one is secure.
formulas.commonMistake: 20 as the FTP CONTROL port - 21 controls, 20 carries data.

formulas.title: Mail Flow Rule

formula.text: SMTP is the only sender; POP3 and IMAP only retrieve.

explanation: Client -> server and server -> server relaying = SMTP.
POP3: download to one device, server copy typically deleted.
IMAP: mail stays server-side; folders sync across devices.
Secure wrappers: SMTPS 465/587, POP3S 995, IMAPS 993.

example.prompt: Read the same inbox on phone and laptop with server folders intact.

formulas.commonMistake: POP3 'syncing' devices - POP3 downloads and deletes.

formulas.title: HTTP vs HTTPS (TLS Wrap)

formula.text: HTTPS adds encryption, integrity and server authentication via certificates.

explanation: HTTP 80 plaintext; anyone on the path reads it.
HTTPS 443: TLS handshake, CA-signed certificate, session keys.
Certificate chain = how the browser authenticates the site.
Methods: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE; codes 200/301/404/500.

steps: TLS certificate verified against a CA chain.

formulas.commonMistake: HTTPS hides the DOMAIN from DNS - it does not; only the content path is encrypted.

formulas.title: TCP Three-Way Handshake

formula.text: Three exchanges open every TCP connection before data flows.

explanation: Client SYN: 'start?'.
Server SYN-ACK: 'yes, and acknowledged'.
Client ACK: session established.
Teardown: FIN/ACK pairs; sequence numbers keep byte order.

example.prompt: Sequence of a TCP connection open?

formulas.memoryTip: S-SA-A: 'Should we? - Sure, and you? - Agreed.'
formulas.commonMistake: ACK-SYN as one message from the client - the SYN-ACK comes from the SERVER.

formulas.title: Support Protocol Purposes

formula.text: Five support protocols, five one-line purposes.

explanation: DNS 53: resolve names to IPs (UDP queries, TCP zone transfers).
DHCP: DORA - Discover Offer Request Ack - leases addresses.
ARP: who-has-this-IP -> MAC mapping on the LAN.
ICMP: echo request/reply (ping) and error reporting.
SNMP 161: monitoring and managing devices.
formulas.commonMistake: Ping on UDP - it rides ICMP, which is neither TCP nor UDP.

tcp-vs-udp-table.q: Which transport opens a session with a handshake?
s: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK = TCP connection setup.

tcp-vs-udp-table.q: Which transport would carry a DNS query by default?

s: Sequence numbers + ACKs reorder and retransmit.

tcp-vs-udp-table.q: Retransmission of lost segments is a feature of:

s: SMTP = TCP 25 - mail must arrive complete.
Realtime audio tolerates loss, not delay.

tcp-vs-udp-table.q: Zone transfers between DNS servers use:

mail-flow-rule.q: Protocol that RELAYS mail between servers:
Which protocol can NEVER retrieve mail?
Mail arrives on the server but the phone never sees it (IMAP configured). First check:
Sending from a mail CLIENT to the company server uses:

s: TLS wraps and encrypts HTTP on 443.

http-vs-https.q: The browser trusts a site's certificate because it is:
s: Certificate chain to a trusted Certificate Authority.

http-vs-https.q: Which HTTP method fetches a page?

s: No TLS = anyone in the middle reads it.
Certificate proves server identity; user login is separate.

http-vs-https.q: HTTP method to upload/replace a resource:
s: PUT stores the body at the URL.

three-way-handshake.q: First message of a TCP connection:

opts: A session is established before data
three-way-handshake.a: A session is established before data

s: Thousands of uncompleted SYNs queue forever.

three-way-handshake.q: Which protocol does NOT use the handshake?

s: The DHCP lease dance spells DORA.

support-protocols-table.q: 'Who has this IP?' is asked by:
s: ARP broadcast resolves IP->MAC on the LAN.
The client doesn't know a server yet - broadcast.
ICMP type 11 - traceroute builds on it.

opts: RARP is reverse; ARP is IP->MAC

support-protocols-table.q: Traceroute builds its hop list using:
s: Incrementing TTL forces ICMP replies at each hop.

mcqs.q: TCP is best described as:
exp: TCP opens sessions (3-way handshake), orders bytes and retransmits losses - reliable at a cost.

mcqs.q: UDP is best described as:
exp: UDP fires datagrams without handshake or retry - fast, minimal overhead.

mcqs.q: The TCP three-way handshake sequence is:
exp: Client SYN -> server SYN-ACK -> client ACK opens the session.

mcqs.q: Which port does HTTP use?
exp: HTTP = 80; HTTPS = 443.

mcqs.q: Which port does HTTPS use?
exp: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS on 443.

mcqs.q: SMTP uses port:
exp: SMTP sends/relays mail on 25.

mcqs.q: POP3 retrieves mail on port:
exp: POP3 = 110; IMAP = 143; IMAPS = 993.

mcqs.q: Which protocol SENDS email?
exp: SMTP = Simple Mail TRANSFER Protocol - the only sender of the three.

mcqs.q: Which retrieval protocol keeps mail on the SERVER and syncs across devices?
exp: IMAP = server-side folders synchronised everywhere.
POP3 downloads and typically deletes.

mcqs.q: DNS resolves:
exp: DNS = the Internet's phonebook: name -> IP.

mcqs.q: DNS queries normally ride:
exp: Queries = UDP 53; zone transfers flip to TCP 53.

mcqs.q: DHCP assigns:
exp: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol leases IP config to hosts.

mcqs.q: The ping utility uses which protocol?
exp: Echo request/reply = ICMP - neither TCP nor UDP.

mcqs.q: ARP maps:
exp: 'Who has this IP?' -> MAC answer - local link only.

mcqs.q: FTP's CONTROL channel uses port:
exp: 21 = control, 20 = data - the two-channel design.

mcqs.q: Which is the SECURE replacement for Telnet?
exp: Telnet 23 is plaintext; SSH 22 encrypts the whole session.

mcqs.q: Telnet uses port:
exp: Telnet = 23; SSH = 22.

mcqs.q: TFTP differs from FTP because it:
exp: TFTP = Trivial FTP on UDP 69 - no auth, minimal features, LAN bootstrap use.

mcqs.q: HTTPS provides:
exp: TLS wraps HTTP with confidentiality, integrity and certificate-based server identity.

mcqs.q: Well-known ports occupy the range:
exp: 0-1023 well-known; 1024+ ephemeral/registered.

mcqs.q: SNMP (port 161) is used for:
exp: Simple Network Management Protocol - device monitoring/management.

mcqs.q: An IP address finds a machine; a PORT finds:
exp: IP -> host, port -> application on that host - one machine runs many services.

mcqs.q: Which application naturally uses UDP?
exp: Realtime media prefers UDP speed; retransmitting stale frames is pointless.

mcqs.q: Which application naturally uses TCP?
exp: Files must arrive complete and ordered -> TCP.
DNS/gaming/voice favour UDP.

mcqs.q: DHCP's DORA sequence stands for:
exp: DORA: client Discover broadcast, server Offer, client Request, server Acknowledge - the lease is live.

mcqs.q: DNS zone transfers between servers use:
exp: Big/serial transfers need TCP reliability; queries stay on UDP 53.

mcqs.q: Which FTP port carries the DATA channel?
exp: 21 = control commands; 20 = actual file data.

mcqs.q: SFTP secures file transfer by:
exp: SFTP = SSH File Transfer Protocol - everything inside the encrypted SSH session.

mcqs.q: IMAP's secure port (IMAPS) is:
exp: IMAPS 993; POP3S 995; SMTPS 465/587.

mcqs.q: Which is TRUE about POP3's default behaviour?
opts: It downloads messages and typically deletes the server copy
exp: Post-Office model: collect the letter, box empties - one-device protocol.

mcqs.q: An extended ACL line 'permit tcp any host 1.1.1.1 eq smtp' filters on:
opts: Destination port 25 traffic to that host
exp: 'eq smtp' = destination port 25 - protocol + port filtering is what makes extended ACLs 'extended'.

mcqs.q: Which HTTP status code means 'Not Found'?
exp: 200 OK; 301 redirect; 404 missing; 500 server error.

mcqs.q: Which HTTP method SUBMITS form data?
exp: POST carries data in the request body; GET exposes parameters in the URL.

mcqs.q: During the TLS handshake, the browser verifies the server using:
exp: Certificate chain up to a trusted Certificate Authority authenticates the site.

mcqs.q: Which pair BOTH normally ride UDP?
exp: DNS queries (53) and DHCP both use UDP.
The rest are TCP family.

mcqs.q: TCP guarantees:
opts: Ordered, complete delivery or an error
exp: Retransmission recovers loss; if the connection dies, TCP reports failure - it never silently drops.

mcqs.q: Which port pair is correct?
exp: 22 secure, 23 insecure - adjacent and frequently swapped in options.

mcqs.q: A firewall blocks port 25 outbound from PCs. Which activity breaks?
opts: Direct mail sending to external SMTP servers
exp: Port 25 = SMTP - blocking it stops PCs sending mail directly (a spam-control measure).

mcqs.q: RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) listens on:
exp: RDP = 3389 - Windows remote desktop.

mcqs.q: Which statement about ports 0-1023 is TRUE?
exp: Well-known range binds the famous services; clients use ephemeral ports above 1023.

mcqs.q: Which protocol would a network MANAGEMENT console use?
exp: Simple Network Management Protocol polls device health on UDP 161.

mcqs.q: IMAPS (993) differs from IMAP (143) by:
exp: The S = TLS-wrapped session - same protocol semantics, encrypted transport.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct mail-flow order?
opts: SMTP client->server, SMTP server->server, IMAP/POP3 retrieval
exp: Push via SMTP twice, then pull via IMAP/POP3 - attachments ride inside the mail protocol.

mcqs.q: Which is a connectionless transport?
exp: UDP sends datagrams without any session setup.

mcqs.q: A user can reach a site by IP but not by name. Which service failed?
exp: Name->IP resolution broken = DNS problem; connectivity itself is fine.

mcqs.q: Which protocol reports 'destination unreachable' errors?
exp: ICMP carries control/error messages - type 3 is destination unreachable.

mcqs.q: HTTPS runs over which transport by default?
exp: TLS needs TCP's reliability - HTTPS = TCP 443 (QUIC/HTTP3 over UDP is the modern exception).

mcqs.q: Which port does SMTPS commonly use for submission?
exp: 587 = mail submission with STARTTLS; 465 = implicit TLS; 25 = server-to-server relay.

mcqs.q: A DNS resolver caches a record, then the zone changes. Which mechanism eventually fixes the stale cache?
exp: Every DNS record carries a Time-To-Live; resolvers drop the cache entry when TTL expires.

mcqs.q: Why does DNS use UDP for queries but TCP for zone transfers?
opts: Queries are small single exchanges; zone transfers are large and need TCP reliability
exp: One small Q&A fits one datagram; multi-record transfers need TCP's ordering and retransmission.

mcqs.q: An attacker floods a server with SYNs but never completes handshakes. This targets:
exp: Half-open SYN floods exhaust TCP's pending-connection queue - a classic DoS.

mcqs.q: Which header is SMALLER on the wire?
exp: UDP's 8-byte header vs TCP's 20+ with sequencing/ACK fields - part of UDP's speed.

mcqs.q: A client behind NAT browses two sites simultaneously. The server-side destination ports are both 443, yet replies reach the right browser tab because:
opts: NAT rewrites source ports uniquely per session
exp: NAT tracks unique ephemeral SOURCE ports per session - that mapping routes replies correctly.

mcqs.q: Which sequence correctly matches protocol-transport-port?
exp: SMTP rides TCP 25; DNS queries UDP 53 (TCP only for transfers); HTTP TCP 80.

mcqs.q: An admin must allow ONLY secure remote terminal access. Which port stays open?
exp: SSH 22 encrypted; Telnet 23 exposes everything in plaintext - close it.

mcqs.q: Which statement about ephemeral ports is TRUE?
opts: Clients pick temporary high ports (1024+) for their side of a connection
exp: Well-known ports bind servers; clients grab ephemeral ports per session.

mcqs.q: A mail client must SEND while the network blocks outbound 25 but allows 587. The fix is:
opts: Use SMTP submission on 587 with STARTTLS
exp: 587 is the modern submission port with STARTTLS - exactly why ISPs block 25 for clients.

mcqs.q: Which protocol pair BOTH use two-channel or multi-message designs?
exp: FTP splits control/data ports; TCP opens with a 3-message handshake - both are multi-message designs.

mcqs.q: An organisation scans its egress and finds PCs hitting random external servers on port 25. Most likely:
exp: Mass outbound SMTP from clients is classic spam-bot behaviour - legitimate clients use 587 via their provider.

mcqs.q: Order these by OSI layer, lowest first: ARP, TCP, HTTP, IP.
exp: ARP = L2 (link), IP = L3 (network), TCP = L4 (transport), HTTP = L7 (application).
Layer-ordering questions compress the whole model into one item.
